In Logistics & Supply Chain, quantum & advanced compute is the frontier tower, run with a pragmatist's discipline. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: quantum readiness & strategy, quantum optimization for enterprise problems, post-quantum cryptography migration — delivered on Dataq Quanta and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Dynamic routing across thousands of stops hits classical solver ceilings in the time available.
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

Services we deploy in this sector

items: A quantum plan that survives a CFO: inventory, risk clocks and sequenced roadmaps.
Routing, scheduling, portfolios and formulations: hybrid solvers beating classical baselines.
Beat the harvest-now-decrypt-later clock: cryptographic inventory to PQC cutover.
QML and simulation pilots with industrial honesty: real baselines, real data, real verdicts.
Quantum-inspired vs. Classical on daily dispatch formulations (route cost down where solvers win)

Intercepted in transit, not at claims

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CMR/ADR/IMDG transport rules and Customs/security regimes (AEO, C-TPAT). Chain-security compliance evidence. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The weekly rhythm below is identical across programs of this type. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
